niche: an intergovernmental liability risk pool setting its 2027 per-occurrence retention from the ground-up severity of its members' liability occurrences, which the pool sees only above each member's deductible and records only up to its own limit

spine.entity: one liability occurrence the pool handled (above its member's deductible), with the member's deductible and the pool's paid and reserved amounts

world.geography: United States (a fictional intergovernmental risk pool of Washington cities and special districts)
world.org_type: intergovernmental risk pool of cities and special districts

driver: The decisive quantity is the upper tail of a size distribution whose items reach the record only above a floor that differs from item to item and are recorded only up to a ceiling that moved during the record, so the fit has to carry each item's floor as truncation and the ceiling as censoring, both at the cost level the curve is fitted at; fitting the recorded sizes as a complete sample thins the tail and sets the dial two steps too low, and treating only the ceiling still leaves it a step and more short.
driver_concrete: Ground-up liability severity is fitted at 2027 cost to the closed occurrences of accident years 2014 to 2021 with each occurrence left-truncated at the deductible its member carried on the date of loss and the occurrences that reached the pool's retention right-censored there, both thresholds brought to 2027 cost with the claim cost index; the expected 2027 occurrences above each quoted attachment (the actuary's count above $25,000 times the fitted tail ratio) first fall to one at $4.0 million, while the lognormal fitted to the recorded costs as complete clears one at $2.0 million and the fit censoring only the capped occurrences at $2.5 million.
stump: The default path brings each closed occurrence's recorded ground-up cost (deductible plus pool paid) to 2027 cost and fits the policy's lognormal by maximum likelihood as a complete sample, which thins the tail and ends on $2.0 million; treating the occurrences stopped at the retention as censored ends on $2.5 million; carrying each deductible as truncation as well files $4.0 million.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field and every filed rule, brings each occurrence to 2027 cost and fits the policy's lognormal by maximum likelihood to the recorded ground-up costs files $2.0 million, and even with the occurrences at the retention treated as censored files $2.5 million, because the record holds only occurrences that exhausted their member's deductible and the easy fit reads that window as the whole curve.
domain_test: The call turns on the ground-up severity distribution of liability occurrences, estimated the way loss models are fitted to insurance data observed through deductibles and policy limits (a truncated and censored likelihood with each observation's own thresholds at the fitted cost level), and on its tail at each quoted attachment; with another field's nouns there is no deductible below which losses never reach the record, no retention at which they stop being recorded, and no excess attachment to set, so the task stops reading the same.
